about: J-Class 14, step 2: Bluebonnet's shipkit build cut into the four parts the game hangs a boat on (ASailboatPawn::ModelMeshesFor: SM_<Tag>_Hull, _Mast, _Boom, _Rudder in /Game/Boats/Bluebonnet), for export_game.py. Body frame metres (X forward, Y starboard, Z up, origin on the load waterline at the middle of the waterline: her physics' frame too). Which of build_jclass.py's objects go in each part, how the moving ones are posed, the game slot (MI_Boat_*) of each of the build's materials, what stays out and why, and the points the game reads (sockets). Edit this file, never the FBX.

SM_Bluebonnet_Hull.note: Everything fixed to the hull, on deck and above it. The pivot is the body frame's origin. Nanite (import_boats.py). The stowed spinnaker pole lies on deck; the runners and checkstays are in the mast's part.

SM_Bluebonnet_Mast.note: The mast with its standing rigging as built (three spreader sets, cap shrouds, intermediates, lowers, jumpers, the forestay, the topmast stay and backstay) and the runners and checkstays, both let off: the game draws no live standing rigging for her (no ForestayTack, ChainplateUpper or BackstayPlate sockets), so nothing is drawn twice. The pivot is the mast's partners, at the physics' MastX on the deck (MastStep). The mast's slot is M_BoatMast's (MastAluminium), kept unpacked, and her bend is held at zero in the game (her wires and fittings would not bend with it), so the part is Nanite (import_boats.py nanite_mast): with her rigging it is 95k triangles, past the 40k a non-Nanite part may have.

SM_Bluebonnet_Boom.note: The boom in its rest pose (its 'frame' from the build: along the centreline), about its own pin, the rest frame's origin (x 2.3508, z 3.7298), which is the physics' gooseneck (MainLuffX since J-Class upwind; BoomZ): the game turns the boom about that point with the physics' boom angle and draws the mainsail's cloth from the same point.

SM_Bluebonnet_Rudder.note: The rudder (the keel's after part) and its stock, about the point where the stock's axis meets the load waterline. The axis is raked 39 degrees aft; the game turns the part about it (RudderAxis, a second point up the axis, BoatModelVisuals.cpp).

SM_Bluebonnet_Wheel.note: The wheel (its rim and spokes, the hub and its shaft) about the hub's centre on the shaft's axis (wheel_hub: the build's 'Wheel' frame, deck_bluebonnet.json steering.wheel). The game turns it about the shaft (WheelHub to WheelAxis on the hull) with the rudder, the top to starboard as the bow goes to starboard (deck.py steering()), and the helm's hands take its rim (WheelRim gives the radius). Nanite (import_boats.py: imported because its origin is in the sockets json).

materials.note: Each of the build's materials to a slot of the game's boat library (make_materials.py BOAT_LIBRARY: MI_Boat_<slot>); pack_slots folds the packed ones (Tools/blender/boat_packs.json). The paint takes the livery's colours (Inputs/g3/boat-catalogue.json, class bluebonnet): the lead keel is painted with the bottom, so it is Antifouling and the canoe slots close (PackCanoe: the volume the tests measure). Her spars are buff paint over the library's Aluminium entry (PaintSpars; the game paints her hull's entry too, for the stowed pole). J-Class 15 (docs/jclass-15): her bronze, manila and varnished teak are her own library slots (CastBronze and Manila with her own detail maps from Inputs/jclass-detail, VarnishedTeak at her build's teak colour), unpacked; the gilt stays Brass. Her teak is LaidTeak (kind 18, unpacked): the export keeps the deck's Planking and Margin maps as UV2 and UV3 and the Aft map's DA in UV1.y on its faces, from which the material draws the planks, seams, butts, king plank and covering boards (laid_deck).

laid_deck.note: J-Class 15 (docs/jclass-15): the after margin's mitre with the covering board (deck.py after_mitre: a D - b DA), as her build reports it (build.json deck.planking_mitre); make_materials.py sets it on MI_Boat_LaidTeak (LaidD) with deck_bluebonnet.json's planking, and the export stops if the build's differs.

left_out.Hull: slice 1's moulded hull, hidden in the build: the fairness check's reference
left_out.*_Light: the build's light copies (slice 12): the game makes its own Nanite fallback (6% of the triangles)
left_out.Mainsail.*, Genoa.*, Quadrilateral.*, St: the game draws her sails as cloth from the physics' strips (FSailCloth)
left_out.Running.*: the running rigging as set for one suit and tack; the game draws her sheets live from the sockets (jib sheets, mainsheet). Her halyards are not drawn yet
left_out.Runner.*.Set, Checkstay.*.Set: the set states: the part carries both pairs let off
left_out.Burgee.*, Ensign.Moored: the game flies its own masthead fly
left_out.Cowls.Moored, CowlCaps.<other suits>: in harbour the cowls stand; at sea the caps (one copy, the genoa suit's) are on
left_out.Below.*, Aft.*: below decks (slices 9 and 10): not in the game yet

sockets.note: The points the game reads, by part (owner). 'at' is a fixed point; 'z_top' puts the height on the top of the named objects' vertices within 'r' (plan) of the point, plus 'dz'; 'z_bottom' on their bottom, plus 'dz'; 'rudder_axis_z' puts the point on the rudder's stock axis at that height (a number, or the top of an object); 'wheel_at' [along, up] puts it 'along' metres forward up the wheel's shaft from the hub and 'up' metres up the king spoke (the build's 'Wheel' frame). Each is checked to lie within 'within' of the named 'near' object's surface, so a change to the build that moves a fitting stops the export. No crew sockets: the game derives her crew's places from the physics' deck (CrewMotion.cpp).

MastStep.why: the mast's partners: the mast part's origin, at the physics' MastX on the deck

RudderPivot.why: where the stock's axis meets the load waterline: the rudder part's origin

RudderAxis.why: a second point up the raked stock: the game turns the rudder about the line between the two

JibLead_S.why: the genoa sheet's lead block on its car (running_bluebonnet.json)

JibWinch_S.why: the primary winch's drum, where the sheet goes on

JibTailer_S.why: the top of the primary, where the tail comes off to the trimmer

JibTailRest_S.why: where the tail lies on deck with no hand on it: aft and inboard of the winch

LazySheetVia.why: the lazy sheet's way across: the game moves it aft to the genoa's clew (aft of the mast), and at this height it clears the doghouse's roof (2.25 m) on its way to the lead

Traveler_C.why: the mainsheet's after deck block on the counter: the game's mainsheet ends here (its car, a small box, sits inside the block)

Traveler_S.why: 1 cm along: she has no traveller, so the game's car stays in the block

MastBase.why: on the mast's axis just above the deck: the mainsail's spreader obstacle runs from here to the hounds

Hounds.why: the forestay's tang on the mast's front: over the genoa's head, so the game keeps the genoa's own head height

SpreaderTip_S.why: the lowest spreader's tip, where the cap shroud crosses it: the mainsail's cloth is kept off the spreader

Boom_Mainsheet.why: under the boom's after mainsheet band (the mainsheet's upper end)

WheelHub.why: the wheel's hub on its shaft's axis: the wheel part's origin

WheelAxis.why: a point 25 cm forward up the shaft (inside it, toward the wheel box): the game turns the wheel about the line from WheelHub

WheelRim.why: the rim's centre line at its top with the king spoke upright (steering.wheel radius 0.6): the game reads the rim's radius from it and puts the helm's hands on the rim

TillerEnd.why: the helm's hand on the wheel: on the stock's axis at the rim's top (10 cm forward of the rim's plane) so it stays put as the rudder turns

RudderStock.why: the stock's head under the deck
